title: A Tracked Vehicle and Its Slip: The Thrust a Track Gets From Soil, the Slip It Costs, and What a Little More Slip on One Side Does to a Straight Line

questions.question: Why must a track slip to give thrust?
options: The motor cannot hold a steady speed
The thrust is the reaction to shearing the soil, and shearing is a slip
Soil always moves under any load
questions.explanation: The soil pushes back only as much as it is sheared, so thrust is zero at no slip and rises with it toward the most the soil can give.

questions.question: On the loose sand, half the largest thrust came at a slip of:
questions.explanation: The curve is steep at first and flat at the end. Half of the most the sand can give came at a tenth of slip.

questions.question: A pivot needed how much a track?
options: 81.8 N, the same as four wheels
32.7 N, against 81.8 N for four wheels
questions.explanation: A track's weight is spread along its length, nearer the middle on average than four wheels at the corners, so less of it has to be dragged far.

questions.question: Slips of 10 and 20 percent on the two tracks turned a straight command by:
questions.explanation: Both tracks were driven at 0.3 m/s. The one slipping 20 percent covered less ground and the vehicle turned toward it.

questions.question: Why can a heading not be held by sending equal commands to two tracks?
options: The two motors are never identical
The slips need not be equal: ground varies from side to side
questions.explanation: A rut or a wet patch under one track changes its slip. Equal commands then give unequal ground speeds, so the heading has to be measured and fed back.

questions.question: Why are the soil values of the lesson marked typical?
options: They are textbook values for a kind of soil, not those of the soil the robot will drive on
They were measured on another vehicle
They are rounded to two digits
They change with the track's speed
questions.explanation: Cohesion, friction angle and shear modulus are the figures for a kind of soil. The ground under a real robot has to be measured.
